component.name: Glimmerwood
component.summary: The web browser that's on your side

description.p: Glimmerwood is a quiet web browser with a small living companion. The wisp, a glowing flame with a friendly face, notices how your time online really feels: it brightens somewhere that restores you, clouds over during a long scroll, and perks up again when you step away. It never blocks a page or scolds you.

ul.li: Hover the wisp to see, in plain words, what is moving it
Home: a garden that grows on good days and never wilts, a greeting that notices what went well, and good places to go
The wisp's days: today, the week and the weeks before, with no minutes or scores
About 2,300 sites sorted by published research on wellbeing online, and yours to change
Private by design: nothing leaves your computer, and the addresses you visit are never recorded

screenshot.caption: The wisp, bright on a page that restores you
Home, with a garden that grows on good days

description.p: Three things the Windows build was doing that it shouldn't.

ul.li: No console window opens beside the browser, and a start that fails says why rather than closing without a word
The engine keeps its profile with everything else Glimmerwood keeps, not in the folder the program was unpacked into
The wisp stays on the toolbar's corner instead of being sent to the corner of the desktop

description.p: The tab column can be dragged on all three systems, and is remembered where you leave it.

ul.li: Drag the edge between the column and the page: narrow for marks alone, wider for titles, and it opens where you left it
How narrow and how wide it may be is decided once, so the three agree
On Windows the wisp follows the system's dark clothes, which it had been assuming the answer to

description.p: Three things the macOS build was missing, two of which Windows was missing as well.

ul.li: The wisp notices that someone is there: neither shell was telling the companion about input, so it slept through whatever you were doing
The macOS app has an icon
The tab column opens wide enough to read a title, and Home and Settings wear the wisp on macOS as they do elsewhere

description.p: Home's forgetting block sits with the week above it rather than beside it.
A restored tab comes back as its title rather than its address.
The Windows build gets what 0.8.0 gave the other two.

ul.li: Downloads, a week of pages, and the tabs you left open coming back asleep, on Windows as well

description.p: The everyday basics, on all three systems at once: downloads, the tabs you left open, and a week of where you've been.

ul.li: Downloads save to your Downloads folder without overwriting what is there, with a quiet mark while one arrives and a line on Home until you open it
The tabs that were open come back asleep: a row in the column with its title, loading nothing until you ask for it
A week of pages, and no longer, kept apart from anything the wisp knows; sites on the private list are never written down
No completion as you type, and there won't be. Ctrl or Cmd with Enter turns a bare word into its .com

A way back out of a stretch you didn't mean to spend: forget the last 15 minutes, half hour, hour or two, which takes those pages, the finished downloads, and the sites out of the wisp's memory of it. How the time felt stays, because that part has to be true

description.p: The macOS and Windows builds are browsers now, on the same core as the Linux one.

ul.li: Tabs, bookmarks, find in page, the keyboard and the wisp in its nook on all three systems
The wisp is drawn on macOS for the first time, at the screen's own scale, following the system's light and dark and holding still when less motion is asked for
Home and Settings do what their buttons say everywhere, and a page that won't open says why in plain words rather than showing the engine's error
A certificate that doesn't check out is named as such, and is never quietly retried without encryption
How large a site is drawn is remembered per site, on Ctrl or Cmd with plus, minus and zero
Each window opens the size it was left

description.p: The wisp does its real work on Windows and macOS, and the welcome page has things to do.

ul.li: The Windows and macOS builds run the same dose engine, lists and history as the Linux one: the wisp watches, takes ratings and keeps its own memory there too
Home and Settings open on all three
The welcome page has a fact worth knowing, with the study named, more good places to walk on through, and a game of catch with the wisp
That page reads properly on a phone, and its home-screen icon survives being cut to a circle
Downloads for Windows and macOS beside the Flatpak, with what to do about the warnings an unsigned app gets

description.p: The wisp reads from across the room, the garden follows the real sun, and there's a page for your phone.

ul.li: The wisp has eyebrows: its mood now reads at a glance rather than only up close
Its nook takes on the weather of your dose, fresh while you recover and dusky while it wears
The garden is lit by where the sun actually is where you are, not by the clock
The wisp follows only the tab in front of you, and sound there keeps you present for half an hour after you last touched anything
A welcome page on the web for phones, which can't run the browser: the same garden, the same good places, and the wisp asleep because it has nothing to watch there
Early Windows and macOS builds, which open a page but are not browsers yet

description.p: Fresh good places, and far more of the web rated.

ul.li: Home's good places come from over 300 researched places, picked afresh every two hours to suit the time of day, the season and how the wisp is
About 8,000 rated sites, up from 2,300, including the 10,000 most-visited sites checked one by one
AI companion apps and gore sites now count as strongly draining
On sites where someone may be in crisis, the wisp stays close and quietly offers a way to talk to someone

description.p: Settings, and a wisp that asks how new places leave you.

ul.li: On a site that's on none of its lists, the wisp asks once how the place leaves you, with a slider from drains me to restores me
A Settings page (Ctrl+comma) to look up and rate any site, change your ratings, choose when the night starts and ends, and see every keyboard shortcut
Ratings are kept in your own reputation.toml, and comments you write there by hand are kept

description.p: Wisp is now called Glimmerwood, since another web browser already goes by Wisp. The companion is still the wisp.

ul.li: A new app ID, io.github.peterwalker78.Glimmerwood, so it installs beside Wisp 0.1.0 rather than over it
Settings, history and bookmarks live under glimmerwood instead of wisp
The wisp, with its moods, moss and a caption that explains what moves it
Home with its garden, greeting, good places, bookmarks and the wisp's days
Tabs in a resizable column, find in page, HTTPS first and tracking protection
